mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk appetite and compressed credit spreads.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the 1-month post-tightening window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% coincides with a 5-day S&P 500 forward return decline as higher labor market rigidity reduces corporate investment expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or non-negative in >70% of similar monthly UNRATE >5% events (binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by more than 8% in the prior quarter, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as excess demand supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 8% in the prior quarter
regime_hint: Economic expansion with output gap expansion
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in >50% of such events (conditional on the output gap signal).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 10% followed by a rise in HOUST above 1000 suggests supply-side weakness, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as valuations adjust higher.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines >10% for two consecutive months then HOUST rises above 1000 in the third month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during validated supply contraction episodes (Granger causality test).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting expectations of accommodative policy and risk-on sentiment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% for three consecutive months and not in recession regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such periods (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS below 130,000 coinciding with a 2% increase in UNRATE predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightening dampens consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 130,000 and UNRATE increases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such labor market events (event study).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of GDPC1 to INDPRO falls below 1.1 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative due to over-supplied conditions and compression in valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 / INDPRO < 1.1 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during validated over-supply periods (regression discontinuity).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL below 210 (monthly) in a non-inflationary regime triggers a 20-day S&P 500 forward return decline as markets anticipate future rate hikes and inflation control.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 210 and inflation < 2% in prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such CPI shocks (robustness check).
